first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are internal funnel decay, and the inherited record most directly on point is memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve), reinforced by memory_31. That is the cheapest lever that plausibly moves both declining metrics at once, and unlike discounting it does not mortgage revenue quality. I am verifying memory_73 first because it is the memory that would otherwise dominate this decision — the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the obvious pull, and memory_73's summary is unusually broad (acquisition lift AND revenue lift AND faster time-to-first-value AND holding across both billing plans). Claims that sweeping are exactly the ones that tend to be over-consolidated from a narrower original result; I want the source record to see the actual segment, duration, and whether 'revenue lift' was gross bookings or net of discount, and whether retention/expansion was ever measured. If the original shows a durable net-revenue effect, promotional_pricing becomes the right response to the competitive threat and I would switch. I am verifying memory_86 second because it is the memory I intend to act on, and its summary is also loose — 'across self-serve accounts' may mean the lift was measured on completion rate, a proxy, rather than on downstream qualified revenue. Downstream value risk is real on both paths and I am flagging it: promotional pricing plausibly buys price-sensitive accounts that churn or never expand, which is acquisition that looks like growth and is not sustainable qualified revenue; and simplification-by-field-removal (memory_31's mechanism) can degrade the qualification data that memory_44's enterprise sales-assist routing depends on, converting qualified pipeline into unrouted self-serve signups. So if I run onboarding simplification I want it shortening steps and deferring fields rather than deleting qualification signal, with enterprise routing held out. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is 3-8 weeks stale against a changed competitive environment, and the observed declines may share a common upstream cause (e.g., traffic mix shifting toward the competitor's price-sensitive segment) that no funnel fix addresses. I hold all of this provisionally pending the two archive pulls.
